quizzes.stem: Two versions of a support assistant both score 92 percent on the evaluation set. One of them gets refund answers wrong far more often, and a wrong refund answer costs twenty times a wrong status answer. What should the report show?

options.a: Accuracy by type of case, with each mistake priced
options.b: The overall accuracy alone, as the two scores are equal
options.c: The average latency, as users notice speed before all else
options.d: The size of the set, as a larger set makes the score fair

explanation.a: A table by segment with the cost of the errors shows the regression that the overall figure averages away.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Equal overall scores can hide unequal failures".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A figure from another dimension cannot stand in for the segment that is failing".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "More cases make the score steadier and do not show where it is low".

quizzes.stem: A team grades a research assistant's free-form reports only with exact-match checks, and the score barely moves when the quality of the reports visibly changes. Which addition fits best?

options.a: A longer answer key, so that more phrasings of each answer count as a match
options.b: Human review of every report, since people are the only judges whose verdict is valid, whatever the cost in time
options.c: A rubric-driven model judge, with people sampling its misses
options.d: Fewer test cases of higher quality, each of them graded by hand with great care

explanation.c: Free text has no single correct form, so a rubric grader scales and people sample for what it misses.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Exact match suits answers with one correct form and rejects a correct report that is worded differently".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Human review of every output does not scale".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the documentation advises "More questions with slightly lower signal automated grading is better than fewer questions with high-quality human hand-graded evals".

quizzes.stem: A new prompt is tried on 80 live cases in each arm and scores five points higher than the current one. What should the team conclude?

options.a: Adopt the new prompt, since five points is the larger number
options.b: Too small a sample to tell, so gather the planned numbers
options.c: Rerun the same 80 cases and average the two results
options.d: Extend the test only if the new prompt is behind

explanation.b: With 80 cases in an arm the gap is inside chance, so the verdict is that there are too few cases.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The larger number is not the better version".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Running the same cases again repeats the same sample and adds no information".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Stopping or extending a test according to who is ahead produces false wins".

quizzes.stem: A new model version matches the current one on overall accuracy in a shadow run. It gains answers in order status and loses answers in refunds, an area the team guards. What does the gate do?

options.a: Ship it to everyone, because the overall totals are equal and the gains in one segment cover the losses in another
options.b: Average the accuracy of the two segments and ship if that average has risen
options.c: Ship it to half of the live traffic and watch whether any customers complain
options.d: Hold the change, since the costly segment regressed and improvements elsewhere cannot pay for that

explanation.d: The gate has a key for guarded segments, and a loss there blocks the change.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A gain in one segment does not pay for a loss in another".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A change that ships to half of the traffic exposes half of the users to the regression before anyone has measured it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "An average of segment accuracies weights a rare segment like a common one and hides its price".

quizzes.stem: A reply to a policy question is confident and wrong. The right passage was not among the chunks the model was given. Which first step fits?

options.a: Lower the temperature so the wording stops varying
options.b: Move the question to a larger model that knows more
options.c: Inspect the index and how the documents are split
options.d: Add examples of confident replies to the prompt

explanation.c: The evidence was never retrieved, so the index and the splitting of documents are the cheapest place to look.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A larger model does not know a document it was never shown".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Sampling settings change how an answer is worded and not what evidence it was given".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Examples teach a format; they do not supply a missing fact".

quizzes.stem: A team's check for its research agent demands exactly three searches in a fixed order, and it fails runs that reach the right answer by another route. What should the check judge instead?

options.a: Whether the runs repeated the same steps, because identical steps prove reliability
options.b: Whether the outcome is correct, then whether the process was sensible
options.c: The number of tool calls, since fewer calls mean a better agent
options.d: The final text, without any look at how it was reached

explanation.b: "Even with identical starting points, agents might take completely different valid paths to reach their goal", so the rule is "Check that the result is right, then check that the process was reasonable".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an eval that checks for a prescribed sequence of steps fails correct runs".
explanation.c: Ruled out because tool efficiency is only one of "five criteria (factual accuracy, citation accuracy, completeness, source quality and tool efficiency)".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the rule is to "check that the process was reasonable" after the result.

quizzes.stem: A team delays building graded examples until it can afford several hundred of them, and early prompt changes are judged by feel. What does the research team's experience suggest?

options.a: Test on the examples written in the prompt
options.b: Wait until the full set has been built
options.c: Judge by feel until launch, then measure
options.d: Start now with a small set of real queries

explanation.d: Early changes are large, so a small set shows them.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "We often hear that AI developer teams delay creating evals because they believe that only large evals with hundreds of test cases are useful", which the team found untrue.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "every week without an eval is a week of judging by feel".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the set should "mirror your real-world task distribution", and "The examples written into a prompt are not that distribution".
